source: Current 62-deck M5 triage and locked canonical engineering decklists
reviewer: ChatGPT; original author, not independent Pass C

rows.reason: Obeka turns vulnerable end-step delayed triggers into permanent resources or safe risky extra turns. Godo is an Equipment tutor and combat enabler but no documented commander-specific delayed liability is created by merely casting it.
rows.positive: Godo finds equipment on entering and might provide repeat attacks with combat setup; a specifically verified Helm of the Host line could produce win pressure if both cards were present.
rows.cut_cost: One-mana Gamble is an exceptionally low-cost tutor for final Fortune, Isochron Scepter, haste and delayed-trigger engines even though it discards randomly.
rules: Obeka ends the turn only when her tapped activated ability resolves, exiling spells and abilities on stack.
Extra-turn lose-game triggers should be put on the stack before ending the turn; premature activation does not permanently suppress future end-step triggers.
Godo tutors Equipment on creature entry; that ability does not by itself repeat delayed triggers.
Godo's first attack extra-combat effect benefits Samurai and equipment lines, not automatically Obeka's key delayed-loss timing.
An equipment-based Godo kill requires actual supporting equipment and accessible mana, neither inferred from M5 combo indexing.
rows.next: Verify all Godo/Helm cards in exact approved 99, and source-paid delayed-trigger turn versus Gamble tutored Final Fortune.

rows.reason: Doctor Doom converts separately discarded land cards into opponent life loss and recycles the lands; an eight-mana generic cast-spell bounce creature does not generate land-discard events.
rows.positive: A paid Tidespout can bounce opposing permanents and sometimes recycle own discard enablers if sufficient spells remain.
rows.cut_cost: Feed the Swarm is affordable black removal of enemy enchantments or creatures, crucial for keeping discard outlets and graveyard recursion operational.
rules: Doom's payoff requires discarding land cards, not casting generic spells.
Tidespout triggers on its controller casting spells, which creates bounces rather than land discard.
Tidespout does not itself retrigger Seismic Assault unless lands are discarded through a separate effect.
Feed the Swarm can target an opposing enchantment, an uncommon role in black removal.
A costed eight-mana creature is not interchangeable with an early sorcery-speed answer.
rows.next: Trace an accessible Tidespout plus true land-discard engine turn and opposing-enchantment removal scenarios.

rows.reason: Mairsil's toolbox relies on activated abilities of exiled cage cards. Training Grounds reduces the mana costs of creature activated abilities; Wound Reflection amplifies life loss but does not cheapen or repeat a cage activation.
rows.positive: If Mairsil activates source-listed loss-of-life abilities repeatedly, Wound Reflection may pressure the whole table at end steps.
rows.cut_cost: Training Grounds reduces activation costs (minimum one mana) of Mairsil's copied creature abilities and helps cast follow-up toolbox interactions the deck actually needs.
rules: Mairsil can activate abilities of caged artifact or creature cards as though Mairsil has them, subject to once-per-ability restrictions.
Training Grounds reduces cost only for activated abilities of creatures its controller controls, not spells.
Mairsil is a creature so its activated cage abilities can be discounted unless relevant cost restrictions apply.
Wound Reflection triggers at the beginning of each end step, checking each opponent's life lost this turn; it is not itself an activated ability.
Removing Training Grounds can turn legal mana-positive or mana-neutral cage sequences into mana-negative lines.
rows.next: Build an exact source cage ability/payment ledger with/without Training Grounds and compare Wound Reflection's finite end-step damage.

rows.reason: A Treasure-producing Pirate advances pirate density, but Beckett needs three different Pirates to connect against the same player; a five-mana body without innate evasion is not automatically enough.
rows.positive: Prosperous Pirates adds a Pirate body and two Treasure tokens on ETB, potentially funding interaction and supporting a later three-Pirate assault.
rows.cut_cost: Jeska's Will is a three-mana fast resource spell or impulse refill, unusually important for deploying several evasive pirates in one turn.
rules: Beckett checks three or more Pirates dealing combat damage to the same player during one turn.
Prosperous Pirates' ETB creates two Treasures; tokens are artifacts not Pirates.
The Pirates' body does not itself evade blockers; connection probability matters for the steal trigger.
Jeska's Will can produce mana based on target opponent's hand or exile playable cards, with both modes when a commander is controlled.
Taking a higher creature count is not enough if it delays the three-distinct-Pirates theft threshold.
rows.next: Paired attacker-count and colored-source turns against two blocker densities, including Jeska's Will immediate line.

rows.reason: Tetsuo has an expensive multicolor tap-activated creature-kill engine. Lotus yields three mana of one chosen color but enters at five mana, whereas two-mana Talisman gives an early U or R plus colorless.
rows.positive: Lotus can provide a repeatable three-mana contribution to UBBR Tetsuo activations in a slow board stall, especially black pips if others pay blue/red.
rows.cut_cost: Talisman accelerates earlier, fixes at least one blue or red pip and supports commander deployment; replacing it increases curve by three.
rules: Tetsuo's activation requires UBBR and tapping, so one Gilded Lotus tap for one color does not alone pay all colored pips.
Gilded Lotus costs five mana and taps to add three mana of any one color.
Talisman of Creativity costs two and adds colorless without loss or U/R at a life cost.
Extra untap effects only increase the utility of Gilded Lotus after it resolves and can activate.
Source paid mana/color access must be measured before describing Lotus as an acceleration improvement.
rows.next: Trace Tetsuo source-paid UBBR activations with actual land/color access under Talisman vs Lotus.

rows.reason: Xander's controller wants to cast/reanimate/clone an expensive commander repeatedly. Young Necromancer can return creatures from the graveyard but needs its own entry timing and graveyard resources; Gamble is a cheap tutor for these routes.
rows.positive: Young Necromancer can return a milled Xander or copied pressure creature directly if its specific reanimation condition is met.
rows.cut_cost: One-mana Gamble searches for an arbitrary engine such as Reanimate, Animate Dead, Helm of the Host or haste, with random discard that may help Xander reanimation.
rules: Xander triggers different effects on entering, attacking and dying, so reanimating can realize a commander-specific enter ability.
Young Necromancer enters and can reanimate a creature if graveyard creature-card requirements are paid.
Young Necromancer is not a universal tutor and requires a previously stocked graveyard.
Gamble's random discard happens after the searched card is placed in hand and can put an otherwise useful card into graveyard.
A five-mana creature reanimation swap is slower than a cheap tutor unless special repeatable ETB access is demonstrated.
rows.next: Verify Young Necromancer exact Oracle cost/condition and compare Xander reanimation across paired hands.
